newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - Feb 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- Posts and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo has undertaken to end government guarantees to cover Post Office losses.
- Individuals are expected to be allowed to make their own foreign investments within the next few months, ending decades of being forced to keep all their savings in rands.

- The involvement of former deputy police commissioner Gen Basie Smith and SA Police forensics chief Gen Lothar Neethling in the supply of the base compounds of mandrax and LSD to military front companies was just one of the issues cardiologist Wouter Basson testified about behind closed doors recently.

- The Gauteng office of the restitution commission has received 78 claims against land which now forms part of Garsfontein, an upmarket suburb east of Pretoria which is home to many senior white public servants.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Chris Stals, the Reserve Bank Governor, recommended yesterday that South African residents should be allowed to invest money overseas in the next phase of the government's gradual relaxation of foreign exchange controls.

- A large restructuring of Saflife, the holding company for Capital Alliance, could be on the cards if a proposal to use Saflife as a vehicle for the 2.8 billion rand takeover of JCI, the mining group, is accepted.

- A wholly owned subsidiary of Macmed Health Care, the listed medical products supplier, is claiming 1.3 million rand in damages from Aiken & Peat (now KPMG Aiken & Peat), the auditing firm, in a case being heard in the Cape Supreme Court.
- The rand was unsettled yesterday by speculation that the Reserve Bank was about to pull out of the forward cover market.
SAKE BEELD
- The further relaxation of foreign exchange controls for individuals and emigrants is in sight.
- Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals on Tuesday threw cold water on the prospective that interest rates will be reduced soon.

- Post and Telecommunications Minister Jay Naidoo on Tuesday announced that postal tariffs would increase drastically in 1997 and 1998 to alleviate the current financial quandary of the South African Post Office.
- The sharp decline last year in the value of the rand helped Trencor to increase its earnings by a fifth in the six months to end December.
THE STAR

- Tearful Springbok coach Andre Markgraaff resigned yesterday amid a public outcry over racist comments he made in a recorded telephone conversation with former Griqualand West captain Andre Bester, and admitted he had been told about the tape in November.
- Claims of blackmail erupted in the Griqualand West rugby community last night after the downfall of their hero, Bok supremo Andre Markgraaff.
- Malawian police were interrogating several suspects late yesterday after abducted Timothy Funnell was found in Chirimba, outside Blantyre, on Monday night after a massive three-day hunt for him.
